package.description: Command-line tool that builds small, self-contained Windows installers (Setup.exe).

en-US.description: Command-line tool that builds small, self-contained Windows installers (Setup.exe).
en-US.longDescription:
TigerSetup is a command-line tool that builds Windows installers. Describe your
application in a TigerSetup.toml file, and tiger-setup build produces one
self-contained Setup.exe with a wizard, a quiet mode for automation, upgrade,
repair and uninstall, and no runtime prerequisites on the target machine.

After installing, open Start > TigerSetup > TigerSetup Shell: a command prompt
with tiger-setup ready to use, which opens on a short getting-started summary.
Start > TigerSetup > TigerSetup Help opens the getting-started guide (PDF).

First commands: tiger-setup build TigerSetup.toml, then tiger-setup inspect and
tiger-setup verify on the Setup.exe it built.

TigerSetup installs for the current user by default and adds tiger-setup to
that user's PATH; the PATH entry is optional. Installing for all users asks for
administrator approval. Uninstalling removes everything the installation added,
except a file you changed after installing it.

tiger-setup build contacts the WinGet community catalog only to resolve WinGet
dependencies a package declares (tiger-setup build --offline makes no network
request). The installers it builds download a prerequisite the package
declares, from the WinGet catalog or from the address the package names, only
when the computer lacks it. Reading product metadata from an MSBuild project
needs the .NET SDK. TigerSetup sends no telemetry.

The installers it builds are transactional: an install or upgrade completes or
rolls back, and each installation records what it owns, so upgrade, uninstall
and verification work from what is really installed.
en-US.name: TigerSetup
